claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for this release is policy-compliant and evidentially supported on the basis that aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and rollout monitoring plus rollback controls make launch acceptable despite the known energy-outage-response limitation.
decision_criteria: If the final release artifacts show explicit disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case before launch, certification becomes plausibly compliant on this narrow basis.
If approved risk acceptance specifically covers the exposed energy outage response segment, certification could also be supported without relying solely on disclosure.
If neither disclosure nor segment-specific approved risk acceptance exists, certification is noncompliant under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model card or release record showing explicit disclosure of the energy outage response limitation before launch.
Provide approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses continued exposure of the energy outage response segment, if disclosure is not the chosen control.
Provide the final certification artifact showing whether certification was conditioned on disclosure and who reviewed that condition.
specific_concerns: The affected energy outage response segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The only risk acceptance in the record is a draft with a blank approver line and it does not address the energy outage response exposure.
No admissible evidence shows the required model-card or release-record disclosure was actually included before certification.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record rather than only conditionally compliant if explicit disclosure is added.
That a 9% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring controls are sufficient to mitigate the weakness under policy while the affected use case remains exposed.
That the release record already satisfies the disclosure predicate required for named launch use cases.
